s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core in a patient with immunocompromised state
salient_findings: Tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions
Angioinvasive microbial structures and thrombosed small vessels on histopathology
Sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells
key_facts: Patient has chronic lymphocytic leukemia
Patient has complex karyotype with TP53 mutation and trisomy 12
Patient was receiving zanubrutinib and subcutaneous immunoglobulin replacement
Patient developed grade 4 neutropenia
Patient had a febrile peak
Skin lesions appeared on the lower limbs and then the upper limbs
Histopathological examination showed severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation
Histopathological examination showed minimal necrosis
Histopathological examination showed angioinvasive microbial structures
Histopathological examination showed thrombosed small vessels
Histopathological examination showed sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells

shortlist.label: Mucormycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Angioinvasive microbial structures and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells in histopathological examination are consistent with Mucormycosis, particularly in an immunocompromised patient.

shortlist.label: Aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe diffuse lympho-monocytic inflammation and thrombosed small vessels in histopathological examination could be indicative of Aspergillosis, a common opportunistic infection in immunocompromised patients.

shortlist.label: Fusariosis
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of grade 4 neutropenia and a febrile peak, along with skin lesions, could suggest Fusariosis, which is known to cause disseminated infection in severely immunocompromised patients.

shortlist.label: Scedosporiosis
shortlist.why_kept: The clinical presentation of tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core, particularly in a patient with chronic lymphocytic leukemia, raises the possibility of Scedosporiosis.

shortlist.label: Apophysomyces variabilis infection
shortlist.why_kept: The histopathological findings of angioinvasive microbial structures and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells, in conjunction with the patient's immunocompromised state, make Apophysomyces variabilis infection a plausible diagnosis.

raw.rationale: The presence of angioinvasive microbial structures, thrombosed small vessels, and sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells in the histopathological examination, along with the patient's immunocompromised state due to chronic lymphocytic leukemia and neutropenia, are consistent with Mucormycosis. The appearance of skin lesions with central ulceration and necrotic core also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Aspergillosis
rejected.why: Aspergillosis typically shows septate hyphae, which is not consistent with the pauciseptate hyphae seen in the histopathological examination.

rejected.label: Fusariosis
rejected.why: Fusariosis is less likely given the presence of sporangial-type cells and the specific histopathological features described.

rejected.label: Scedosporiosis
rejected.why: Scedosporiosis is less likely due to the lack of characteristic features such as slender, septate hyphae and the presence of sporangial-type cells in the histopathological examination.

rejected.label: Apophysomyces variabilis infection
rejected.why: While Apophysomyces variabilis is a type of Mucorales, the specific features described in the histopathological examination, such as the presence of sparse hyphal mats with sporangial-type cells, are more consistent with Mucormycosis.
